text: [[selam]]! Today we read the life of one of the greatest saints of Ethiopia, [[tekle-haimanot]]. Read with me, then test yourself!
plain: Selam! Today we read the life of one of the greatest saints of Ethiopia, Tekle Haimanot. Read with me, then test yourself!

text: His parents, Tsega Ze-Ab (Gift of the Father) and Egzi-Haraya (Chosen by God), loved God and were kind to the sick and the poor.
plain: His parents, Tsega Ze-Ab (Gift of the Father) and Egzi-Haraya (Chosen by God), loved God and were kind to the sick and the poor.

text: On the twelfth of every month they kept the feast of [[kidus-mikael]] by feeding the poor. This is called a Zikir.
plain: On the twelfth of every month they kept the feast of Kidus Mikael by feeding the poor. This is called a Zikir.

text: In a vision, the Archangel told them they would have a blessed child, like John the Baptist. He was born on the twenty-fourth of Tahsas, and they named him Fesseha Tsion, the Joy of Zion.
plain: In a vision, the Archangel told them they would have a blessed child, like John the Baptist. He was born on the twenty-fourth of Tahsas, and they named him Fesseha Tsion, the Joy of Zion.

text: Three days after he was born, the Holy Spirit came upon him, and the baby spoke: One is the Holy Father, One is the Holy Son, One is the Holy Spirit!
plain: Three days after he was born, the Holy Spirit came upon him, and the baby spoke: One is the Holy Father, One is the Holy Son, One is the Holy Spirit!

text: Later there was a famine. His parents had little flour and oil left for their Zikir. Tap the jar.
plain: Later there was a famine. His parents had little flour and oil left for their Zikir. Tap the jar.

text: The young boy prayed, and the flour and oil grew, so the poor could still be fed!
plain: The young boy prayed, and the flour and oil grew, so the poor could still be fed!

text: He was ordained a deacon at fifteen. His parents wanted him to marry, but he wished to serve God.
plain: He was ordained a deacon at fifteen. His parents wanted him to marry, but he wished to serve God.

text: One day, while he was out hunting, the Archangel Michael appeared to him and said he would spend his life saving souls. He named him [[tekle-haimanot]], which means Tree of Faith.
plain: One day, while he was out hunting, the Archangel Michael appeared to him and said he would spend his life saving souls. He named him Tekle Haimanot, which means Tree of Faith.

text: He gave his money to the church and the poor, became a monk and a priest, and taught many people who did not know God. In Ketata, he drove out an evil spirit from a tree the people worshipped.
plain: He gave his money to the church and the poor, became a monk and a priest, and taught many people who did not know God. In Ketata, he drove out an evil spirit from a tree the people worshipped.

text: His monastery was on a high cliff, and the monks climbed up and down on a rope.
plain: His monastery was on a high cliff, and the monks climbed up and down on a rope.

text: One day the rope broke! As he fell, he prayed to God. Tap the saint.
plain: One day the rope broke! As he fell, he prayed to God. Tap the saint.

text: God gave him six wings, and he flew down safely!
plain: God gave him six wings, and he flew down safely!

text: That is why icons of [[tekle-haimanot]] show him with wings.
plain: That is why icons of Tekle Haimanot show him with wings.

text: He spent his last twenty-nine years at Debre Asbo, praying standing for a long time. He lost one leg from standing so long, yet he prayed on one leg for seven more years.
plain: He spent his last twenty-nine years at Debre Asbo, praying standing for a long time. He lost one leg from standing so long, yet he prayed on one leg for seven more years.

text: [[selam]]! Adam and Eve broke the one commandment God gave them. What did God do then? Let's find out.
plain: Selam! Adam and Eve broke the one commandment God gave them. What did God do then? Let's find out.

text: God gave Adam and Eve every plant in paradise for food, except one: the tree of knowledge. If you eat of it, you will die. To keep this commandment was their way of loving God.
plain: God gave Adam and Eve every plant in paradise for food, except one: the tree of knowledge. If you eat of it, you will die. To keep this commandment was their way of loving God.

text: Adam and Eve kept the commandment for seven years. Then the devil, hiding in the serpent, came to Eve. Tap the serpent.
plain: Adam and Eve kept the commandment for seven years. Then the devil, hiding in the serpent, came to Eve. Tap the serpent.

text: It said: You will not die. Your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God.
plain: It said: You will not die. Your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God.

text: Eve looked at the tree. It was good for food, pleasant to the eyes, and desirable to make one wise. But she forgot what God had said.
plain: Eve looked at the tree. It was good for food, pleasant to the eyes, and desirable to make one wise. But she forgot what God had said.

text: She ate, and gave to Adam, and he ate too. At once their eyes were opened, and they knew they were naked.
plain: She ate, and gave to Adam, and he ate too. At once their eyes were opened, and they knew they were naked.

text: When they heard God walking in the garden, they were afraid and hid. God called: Where are you? Tap the bushes to find them.
plain: When they heard God walking in the garden, they were afraid and hid. God called: Where are you? Tap the bushes to find them.

text: God already knew where they were. He called them because He is a loving Father, giving them the chance to come back.
plain: God already knew where they were. He called them because He is a loving Father, giving them the chance to come back.

text: Adam! He said: I heard Your voice, and I was afraid, so I hid.
plain: Adam! He said: I heard Your voice, and I was afraid, so I hid.

text: Eve! Before, they loved to be near God. Now sin made them afraid.
plain: Eve! Before, they loved to be near God. Now sin made them afraid.

text: The serpent. The devil had fooled them into sin.
plain: The serpent. The devil had fooled them into sin.

text: God asked Adam: Have you eaten from the tree I told you not to eat from? If you were Adam, what should you say?
plain: God asked Adam: Have you eaten from the tree I told you not to eat from? If you were Adam, what should you say?

text: That is what Adam said. He blamed Eve, and Eve blamed the serpent. No one said sorry. Try the other answer.
plain: That is what Adam said. He blamed Eve, and Eve blamed the serpent. No one said sorry. Try the other answer.

text: That is repentance. Blaming others hides sin; confessing it opens the door to God's mercy.
plain: That is repentance. Blaming others hides sin; confessing it opens the door to God's mercy.

text: Because of sin, death came into the world. God told Adam and Eve: You will return to the dust.
plain: Because of sin, death came into the world. God told Adam and Eve: You will return to the dust.

text: But even then, God gave hope. He said to the serpent: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her Seed.
plain: But even then, God gave hope. He said to the serpent: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her Seed.

text: The woman is the Virgin [[mariam]], and her Seed is our Lord Jesus Christ, who would be born of her to save Adam and all his children. Tap her.
plain: The woman is the Virgin Mariam, and her Seed is our Lord Jesus Christ, who would be born of her to save Adam and all his children. Tap her.
